events.name: ConfigChange
events.when: When a configuration file changes during a session

outputFields.description: `"block"` prevents the configuration change from being applied. Omit to allow the change
Explanation shown to the user when `decision` is `"block"`

events.name: CwdChanged
events.when: When the working directory changes, for example when Claude executes a `cd` command. Useful for reactive environment management with tools like direnv

outputFields.description: Array of absolute paths. Replaces the current dynamic watch list (paths from your `matcher` configuration are always watched). Returning an empty array clears the dynamic list, which is typical when entering a new directory

events.name: Elicitation
events.when: When an MCP server requests user input during a tool call

events.name: ElicitationResult
events.when: After a user responds to an MCP elicitation, before the response is sent back to the server

events.name: FileChanged
events.when: When a watched file changes on disk. The `matcher` field specifies which filenames to watch

inputFields.description: Absolute path to the file that changed
What happened: `"change"` (file modified), `"add"` (file created), or `"unlink"` (file deleted)

outputFields.description: Array of absolute paths. Replaces the current dynamic watch list (paths from your `matcher` configuration are always watched). Use this when your hook script discovers additional files to watch based on the changed file

events.name: InstructionsLoaded
events.when: When a CLAUDE.md or `.claude/rules/*.md` file is loaded into context. Fires at session start and when files are lazily loaded during a session

inputFields.description: Absolute path to the instruction file that was loaded
Scope of the file: `"User"`, `"Project"`, `"Local"`, or `"Managed"`

Why the file was loaded: `"session_start"`, `"nested_traversal"`, `"path_glob_match"`, `"include"`, or `"compact"`. The `"compact"` value fires when instruction files are re-loaded after a compaction event
Path glob patterns from the file's `paths:` frontmatter, if any. Present only for `path_glob_match` loads
Path to the file whose access triggered this load, for lazy loads
Path to the parent instruction file that included this one, for `include` loads

events.name: Notification
events.when: When Claude Code sends a notification
events.inputExample:
{
  "session_id": "abc123",
  "transcript_path": "/Users/.../.claude/projects/.../00893aaf-19fa-41d2-8238-13269b9b3ca0.jsonl",
  "cwd": "/Users/...",
  "hook_event_name": "Notification",
  "message": "Claude needs your permission to use Bash",
  "title": "Permission needed",
  "notification_type": "permission_prompt"
}

events.name: PermissionDenied
events.when: When a tool call is denied by the auto mode classifier. Return `{retry: true}` to tell the model it may retry the denied tool call

inputFields.description: The classifier's explanation for why the tool call was denied

events.inputExample:
{
  "session_id": "abc123",
  "transcript_path": "/Users/.../.claude/projects/.../00893aaf-19fa-41d2-8238-13269b9b3ca0.jsonl",
  "cwd": "/Users/...",
  "permission_mode": "auto",
  "hook_event_name": "PermissionDenied",
  "tool_name": "Bash",
  "tool_input": {
    "command": "rm -rf /tmp/build",
    "description": "Clean build directory"
  },
  "tool_use_id": "toolu_01ABC123...",
  "reason": "Auto mode denied: command targets a path outside the project"
}

events.name: PermissionRequest
events.when: When a permission dialog appears

outputFields.description: `"allow"` grants the permission, `"deny"` denies it. [Deny and ask rules](/en/permissions#manage-permissions) are still evaluated, so a hook returning `"allow"` does not override a matching deny rule

For `"allow"` only: modifies the tool's input parameters before execution. Replaces the entire input object, so include unchanged fields alongside modified ones. The modified input is re-evaluated against deny and ask rules
For `"allow"` only: array of [permission update entries](#permission-update-entries) to apply, such as adding an allow rule or changing the session permission mode
For `"deny"` only: tells Claude why the permission was denied
For `"deny"` only: if `true`, stops Claude

events.name: PostCompact
events.when: After context compaction completes

events.name: PostToolBatch
events.when: After a full batch of parallel tool calls resolves, before the next model call

outputFields.description: Context string injected once before the next model call. See [Add context for Claude](#add-context-for-claude) for delivery details, what to put in it, and how resumed sessions handle past values

events.name: PostToolUse
events.when: After a tool call succeeds

inputFields.description: Optional. Tool execution time in milliseconds. Excludes time spent in permission prompts and PreToolUse hooks

outputFields.description: `"block"` adds the `reason` next to the tool result. Claude still sees the original output; to replace it, use `updatedToolOutput`
Explanation shown to Claude when `decision` is `"block"`
String added to Claude's context alongside the tool result. See [Add context for Claude](#add-context-for-claude)
Replaces the tool's output with the provided value before it is sent to Claude. The value must match the tool's output shape
Replaces the output for [MCP tools](#match-mcp-tools) only. Prefer `updatedToolOutput`, which works for all tools

events.name: PostToolUseFailure
events.when: After a tool call fails

inputFields.description: String describing what went wrong
Optional boolean indicating whether the failure was caused by user interruption
Optional. Tool execution time in milliseconds. Excludes time spent in permission prompts and PreToolUse hooks

events.inputExample:
{
  "session_id": "abc123",
  "transcript_path": "/Users/.../.claude/projects/.../00893aaf-19fa-41d2-8238-13269b9b3ca0.jsonl",
  "cwd": "/Users/...",
  "permission_mode": "default",
  "hook_event_name": "PostToolUseFailure",
  "tool_name": "Bash",
  "tool_input": {
    "command": "npm test",
    "description": "Run test suite"
  },
  "tool_use_id": "toolu_01ABC123...",
  "error": "Command exited with non-zero status code 1",
  "is_interrupt": false,
  "duration_ms": 4187
}

outputFields.description: String added to Claude's context alongside the error. See [Add context for Claude](#add-context-for-claude)

events.name: PreCompact
events.when: Before context compaction

events.name: PreToolUse
events.when: Before a tool call executes. Can block it

outputFields.description: `"allow"` skips the permission prompt. `"deny"` prevents the tool call. `"ask"` prompts the user to confirm. `"defer"` exits gracefully so the tool can be resumed later. [Deny and ask rules](/en/permissions#manage-permissions) are still evaluated regardless of what the hook returns
For `"allow"` and `"ask"`, shown to the user but not Claude. For `"deny"`, shown to Claude. For `"defer"`, ignored

Modifies the tool's input parameters before execution. Replaces the entire input object, so include unchanged fields alongside modified ones. Combine with `"allow"` to auto-approve, or `"ask"` to show the modified input to the user. For `"defer"`, ignored
String added to Claude's context alongside the tool result. Ignored when `permissionDecision` is `"defer"`. See [Add context for Claude](#add-context-for-claude)

events.name: SessionEnd
events.when: When a session terminates

events.name: SessionStart
events.when: When a session begins or resumes

outputFields.description: String added to Claude's context at the start of the conversation, before the first prompt. See [Add context for Claude](#add-context-for-claude) for how the text is delivered and what to put in it

events.name: Setup
events.when: When you start Claude Code with `--init-only`, or with `--init` or `--maintenance` in `-p` mode. For one-time preparation in CI or scripts

outputFields.description: String added to Claude's context. Multiple hooks' values are concatenated

events.name: Stop
events.when: When Claude finishes responding
events.inputExample:
{
  "session_id": "abc123",
  "transcript_path": "~/.claude/projects/.../00893aaf-19fa-41d2-8238-13269b9b3ca0.jsonl",
  "cwd": "/Users/...",
  "permission_mode": "default",
  "hook_event_name": "Stop",
  "stop_hook_active": true,
  "last_assistant_message": "I've completed the refactoring. Here's a summary..."
}

outputFields.description: `"block"` prevents Claude from stopping. Omit to allow Claude to stop
Required when `decision` is `"block"`. Tells Claude why it should continue

events.name: StopFailure
events.when: When the turn ends due to an API error. Output and exit code are ignored

inputFields.description: Error type: `rate_limit`, `authentication_failed`, `oauth_org_not_allowed`, `billing_error`, `invalid_request`, `server_error`, `max_output_tokens`, or `unknown`
Additional details about the error, when available

The rendered error text shown in the conversation. Unlike `Stop` and `SubagentStop`, where this field holds Claude's conversational output, for `StopFailure` it contains the API error string itself, such as `"API Error: Rate limit reached"`

events.inputExample:
{
  "session_id": "abc123",
  "transcript_path": "/Users/.../.claude/projects/.../00893aaf-19fa-41d2-8238-13269b9b3ca0.jsonl",
  "cwd": "/Users/...",
  "hook_event_name": "StopFailure",
  "error": "rate_limit",
  "error_details": "429 Too Many Requests",
  "last_assistant_message": "API Error: Rate limit reached"
}

events.when: When you submit a prompt, before Claude processes it

outputFields.description: `"block"` prevents the prompt from being processed and erases it from context. Omit to allow the prompt to proceed
Shown to the user when `decision` is `"block"`. Not added to context

Sets the session title. Use to name sessions automatically based on the prompt content

events.name: WorktreeCreate
events.when: When a worktree is being created via `--worktree` or `isolation: "worktree"`. Replaces default git behavior

events.name: WorktreeRemove
events.when: When a worktree is being removed, either at session exit or when a subagent finishes

fields.description: Permission rule syntax to filter when this hook runs, such as `"Bash(git *)"` or `"Edit(*.ts)"`. The hook only spawns if the tool call matches the pattern, or if a Bash command is too complex to parse. Only evaluated on tool events: `PreToolUse`, `PostToolUse`, `PostToolUseFailure`, `PermissionRequest`, and `PermissionDenied`. On other events, a hook with `if` set never runs. Uses the same syntax as [permission rules](/en/permissions)
Seconds before canceling. Defaults: 600 for command, 30 for prompt, 60 for agent
Custom spinner message displayed while the hook runs
If `true`, runs once per session then is removed. Only honored for hooks declared in [skill frontmatter](#hooks-in-skills-and-agents); ignored in settings files and agent frontmatter
If `true`, runs in the background without blocking. See [Run hooks in the background](#run-hooks-in-the-background)

If `true`, runs in the background and wakes Claude on exit code 2. Implies `async`. The hook's stderr, or stdout if stderr is empty, is shown to Claude as a system reminder so it can react to a long-running background failure

Shell to use for this hook. Accepts `"bash"` (default) or `"powershell"`. Setting `"powershell"` runs the command via PowerShell on Windows. Does not require `CLAUDE_CODE_USE_POWERSHELL_TOOL` since hooks spawn PowerShell directly
URL to send the POST request to
Additional HTTP headers as key-value pairs. Values support environment variable interpolation using `$VAR_NAME` or `${VAR_NAME}` syntax. Only variables listed in `allowedEnvVars` are resolved
List of environment variable names that may be interpolated into header values. References to unlisted variables are replaced with empty strings. Required for any env var interpolation to work
Name of a configured MCP server. The server must already be connected; the hook never triggers an OAuth or connection flow
Name of the tool to call on that server
Arguments passed to the tool. String values support `${path}` substitution from the hook's [JSON input](#hook-input-and-output), such as `"${tool_input.file_path}"`
Prompt text to send to the model. Use `$ARGUMENTS` as a placeholder for the hook input JSON
Model to use for evaluation. Defaults to a fast model

commonInput.description: Current working directory when the hook is invoked

Current [permission mode](/en/permissions#permission-modes): `"default"`, `"plan"`, `"acceptEdits"`, `"auto"`, `"dontAsk"`, or `"bypassPermissions"`. Not all events receive this field: see each event's JSON example below to check

Object with a `level` field holding the active [effort level](/en/model-config#adjust-effort-level) for the turn: `"low"`, `"medium"`, `"high"`, `"xhigh"`, or `"max"`. If the requested effort exceeds what the current model supports, this is the downgraded level the model actually used, not the level you requested. The object matches the [status line](/en/statusline#available-data) `effort` field. Present for events that fire within a tool-use context, such as `PreToolUse`, `PostToolUse`, `Stop`, and `SubagentStop`, when the current model supports the effort parameter. The level is also available to hook commands and the Bash tool as the `$CLAUDE_EFFORT` environment variable.
Name of the event that fired
Unique identifier for the subagent. Present only when the hook fires inside a subagent call. Use this to distinguish subagent hook calls from main-thread calls.

Agent name (for example, `"Explore"` or `"security-reviewer"`). Present when the session uses `--agent` or the hook fires inside a subagent. For subagents, the subagent's type takes precedence over the session's `--agent` value.
